question: What is the repo rate given by the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) as on 7 April 2021?
solution:
The correct answer is__** ​4%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Current Repo Rate: 6.5 %, Reverse Repo Rate- 3.5 %**
 
• **The Repo rate** is given by the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) as of 7 April 2021 is **4%.**
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) increased the policy repo rate by 40 basis points to** 4.40 per cent w.e.f 21 May 2022.**
 
• The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has unanimously voted to increase the policy repo rate by 40 basis points or 0.40 per cent.
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) raised by **50 bps to 4.50%** effective May 21.
 
• Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) adjusted to** 4.15% while Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) to 4.65%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Repo Rate:

 
 
• ​It is a rate at which the central bank (RBI) lends money to its clients against government securities.
 
 
 
• Reverse Repo:
 
 
• ​It is the rate at which the central bank (RBI) borrows money from its clients.
 
 
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR):
 
 
• The RBI (Amendment) Bill, 2006, empowers RBI to prescribe CRR–Cash that banks deposit with the RBI without any floor rate or ceiling rate.
 
 
 
• Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR):
 
 
• It is the ratio of a liquid asset, which all commercial banks have to keep in the form of cash, gold, and unencumbered approved securities equal to not more than 40% of their total demand and time deposit liabilities (ranges is 25‑40%).
 
 
 
• Bank Rate:
 
 
• It is also called the rediscount rate. It is the rate, at which the RBI gives finance to commercial banks.
